findings.title: The new `user != null` check turns off passkeys on the normal login page.
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `fillContextForm` ran only when no user was selected, i.e. on the ordinary first login page. Both callers (`authenticate` at line 115 and `challenge` at line 137) now skip `fillContextForm` when no user is set. So on a fresh login with no user, the conditional-UI/webauthn form is never set up, and the existing tests that assert `//form[@id='webauth']` on a fresh login would fail.

At the same time, any re-authenticating user gets passkey data, even a user with no passwordless credential. That goes against the new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`.

Fix: `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS));`

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called without an argument, but the only version shown takes a `UserModel`.
findings.body:
`UsernamePasswordForm` defines only `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This call passes no argument, so it will not compile unless there is a no-argument overload I can't see.

The intent also looks wrong. When passkeys are enabled, re-authentication always shows the username form, even when the current user has no passkey. Previously that case returned `success()`.

Fix: pass `context.getUser()`. Then a re-authenticating user without a passkey still skips the form as before.

held.title: During re-authentication the passkey prompt no longer limits which credentials are allowed, so a different user's passkey could be accepted.
held.body:
`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` now always returns false. During re-authentication, when the user is already identified, the form therefore sends no `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` and sets `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false`. The browser can then offer any discoverable passkey for the RP, including one that belongs to another account.

The resulting assertion carries another user's handle. Unless `action()` checks that this user matches `context.getUser()`, re-authentication with `prompt=login` would silently switch the session to that other user. I could not see `action()`, so please confirm such a check exists, or add one that rejects a user handle that differs from the already-set user.
